story.title: About the Madeline Island course
paragraphs: Madeline Island Marathon & Half Marathon takes place in La Pointe, Wisconsin, with both races starting and finishing in front of Joni’s Beach a few blocks from the ferry landing.

The public race information emphasizes a destination weekend: runners are encouraged to arrive Friday, use the Bayfield ferry, stay on or near the island, and celebrate after the race with food, beverage, live music, awards, and a local artisan finisher medal.

faqs.question: How do runners get to Madeline Island?
faqs.answer: Madeline Island is accessible by ferry from Bayfield, Wisconsin. The race page describes a 25-minute ferry ride for passenger, bike, and vehicle transportation, with service dependent on weather.

faqs.question: Will there be an early ferry on race day?
faqs.answer: The public FAQ says the early race-day ferry to the island leaves Bayfield at 6:30 AM, regular service continues after that, and the race starts at 8:30 AM sharp. The ferry is first-come, first-served and weather permitting.

links.label: Madeline Island Ferry schedule and rates

faqs.question: What is included with registration?
faqs.answer: The race page lists a long-sleeve tech shirt, a custom finisher medal created by local artisan Grace Hogan Jewelry, and a free beverage and meal at the post-race party.

faqs.question: Can runners transfer or switch their entry?
faqs.answer: The public FAQ says transfers and distance switches are available through April 16, 2026, with transfer handling through Race Roster and no transfers or switches accepted after that date.

faqs.question: Is there a course time limit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The race page and FAQ state a 7-hour course time limit.

faqs.question: How large is the field?
faqs.answer: The About page says registration for 2026 is limited to 150 in the full marathon and 350 in the half marathon.

travel_logistics.headline: Getting There / Where to Stay
travel_logistics.intro: Plan the island weekend before you register: the race starts and finishes at Joni’s Beach in La Pointe, and most runners build the trip around the Bayfield–La Pointe ferry, lodging availability, and packet pickup windows.

items.label: Getting there
items.title: Take the Bayfield–La Pointe ferry
items.text: Madeline Island is reached by ferry from Bayfield. The race information describes a roughly 25-minute crossing for passengers, bikes, and vehicles, with service first-come, first-served and weather permitting.

items.label: Arrival timing
items.title: Build in ferry and weather buffer
items.text: Arriving Friday keeps packet pick-up, lodging check-in, and ferry timing from competing with the 8:30 AM race start. The published race-day ferry option leaves Bayfield early, but regular ferry service and weather still matter.

items.label: Where to stay
items.title: Stay on or near the island
items.text: The race’s destination-weekend guidance encourages runners to plan lodging early on Madeline Island or nearby Bayfield. Camping can be part of the weekend plan where official lodging resources point runners.

items.label: Packet pickup
items.title: Pick up at Joni’s Beach
items.text: Packet pick-up is listed Friday from 4:00–8:00 PM and race day from 6:30–8:00 AM at the event tent at Joni’s Beach on Madeline Island.

items.label: Start and finish
items.title: Joni’s Beach keeps logistics close
items.text: Both races start and finish in front of Joni’s Beach in La Pointe, a few blocks from the ferry landing, so the race-day plan can stay compact once you are on the island.

destination_gallery.headline: What the island weekend looks like.
destination_gallery.intro: Race day is inseparable from the place: a Bayfield ferry crossing, packet pickup at Joni’s Beach, a La Pointe start/finish, shoreline roads, lodging decisions, and weather-aware island logistics.
